manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the phone on the box and place it on the phone stand to the right.

Task description: Place the white-edged, black-screen phone on the white box at the left onto the silver phone stand to its right, which has a slanted backboard and bottom hooks.

Success criteria: The phone is independently supported by the phone stand and remains stable after the gripper releases it, without slipping or tipping.

## Execution tips

- Consider grasping straight middle frame sections along both long edges of the phone, avoiding side buttons and leaving its lower end free for the stand. Open slightly wider than the body while watching clearance from pens on both sides.
- The phone lies flat against the box. Before closing, use different views to confirm the fingers are on opposite sides and pads can contact the frame, avoiding mere image overlap or fingertips pressing the screen or box and pushing the phone away.
- When adjusting the phone tilt, choose a location clear of the box surface and nearby objects, with room to rotate, reducing the risk of the phone ends or gripper brushing objects on the table.
- Near the phone stand, align the phone back with the backplate tilt and place its lower edge within both support hooks. Leave finger-withdrawal clearance to avoid pressing the phone against the hooks or hitting the backplate and moving the stand.
- Release slowly after the bottom edge is supported by the hook and the back rests against the support plate. Check whether the phone slides or tips, avoiding release before support is established.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start this physical-robot episode with the specified parameters, execute from the returned manual and live observations, then call finish_episode and report the recording directory.

The manual and both camera feeds show the phone lying flat on the left side of the box, with the stand empty on the right. I am adjusting the gripper orientation and lateral position above it; after approaching the phone’s side frame, I will switch to small-step movements.

Adjusting the downward angle hit a controller joint limit; feedback permits replanning within the same episode. I reduced the angle slightly. Next I will adjust position and confirm reachability before continuing the approach.
The gripper is above the phone, aligned across its two long edges. Next I will lower by centimeters, using the frame and nearby pen clearance to confirm the contact height, then close the gripper.

The fingers are close to the phone's side edges near its midpoint. The phone remains flat with no visible movement. I will close slightly and make a short test lift to confirm it leaves the box surface steadily with the gripper.

The first test lift did not confirm a stable grasp; the phone remains on the box surface. I have reopened the gripper and adjusted it slightly lower and sideways so the pads contact the side frame more fully, then will test the lift again.

During this test lift, the phone rose with the gripper, its opening stayed around 74.9 mm and no slipping was visible. I will first increase box clearance, then move toward the right stand and gradually adjust phone tilt.
The phone has left the box and remains grasped. The stand is at an angle, and I am adjusting the phone orientation above it. Near the backboard and hooks, I will continue aligning in small steps.

The phone's edge is roughly parallel to the stand's backboard, and the grasp remains stable. I am beginning to lower in small steps and adjusting the bottom edge relative to the two hooks; I will release after support is established.

The phone is descending in front of the stand, which has not visibly moved, and the phone has not visibly slipped. I have not confirmed that its lower edge is seated in the hook yet, so I will continue checking in small steps.

The phone bottom and back panel occlude each other in the current image, leaving front/back position unclear. I will lift out of this region and adjust toward the stand front to avoid hitting the back panel during further descent.
I lifted higher and left clearance in front of the stand. Next I will correct the offset across the stand's width and descend again; the phone remains securely held.
The lateral offset has decreased, and the phone's bottom edge is now above the hooks. Next I will use smaller lowering and backboard approach movements to check support while maintaining the grasp.

The lower edge is near the support hook, and the stand remains in its original position. I am descending with smaller steps to confirm support on both sides, then will gradually release and observe stability.

After slightly loosening the gripper, the phone lowered a little and stopped on the stand; the image indicates it is supported. I will open the gripper further, withdraw from the contact area, then check whether it remains stable.
The gripper is open and withdrawn; the phone remains supported by the stand, with no slipping or tipping in consecutive observations. I will watch for a few more seconds, then close this episode.
